maps_geocode.purpose: Resolve an address or landmark to the first Geocoding match. Use this to obtain reusable coordinates and a place ID; it does not validate postal deliverability.

address.description: Address, city or landmark to geocode.

maps_geocode.result: An object with `location.lat`, `location.lng`, `formatted_address` and `place_id`. Only the first result is returned.
notes: No match is a tool error, not an empty successful location.
This direct tool uses Geocoding v3; Places fallback is used by location-resolving composites, not by this call.
maps_geocode.authentication: API key required in this implementation.

maps_validate_address.purpose: Validate postal components and return corrections, the standardized address and Google’s verdict. Keep the verdict and unresolved components visible to the caller.

addressLines.description: One or more postal-address lines, in order.

regionCode.description: Two-letter uppercase country/region code; recommended to disambiguate the address.
regionCode.default: Not supplied; Google may infer it

administrativeArea.description: State, province or corresponding administrative area.

enableUspsCass.description: Request USPS CASS processing; this implementation requires regionCode US or PR when true.

sessionToken.description: Same-project Autocomplete (New) session token. Reuse the prediction token in this concluding request; create a fresh token for the next session.
sessionToken.default: No session token; Google bills outside an Autocomplete session

maps_validate_address.result: The complete validation response, typically including `result.verdict`, `result.address`, `result.geocode` and `responseId`; Google may omit unavailable fields.
notes: A validation verdict is not a delivery guarantee.
Region/API coverage varies. This tool does not submit validation feedback or automatically accept corrections.
maps_validate_address.authentication: API key or OAuth for the main API.

maps_pollen.purpose: Retrieve a short daily pollen forecast for exact coordinates. The response preserves pollen types, indices, plant information and provider recommendations.

latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

days.description: Number of daily forecast records to request.

plantsDescription.description: Include detailed plant descriptions and related information when available.

maps_pollen.result: The original Pollen response, including `regionCode`, `dailyInfo` and any `nextPageToken`. Each day can include pollen-type and plant information.
notes: Requests use a page size of 5, sufficient for this tool’s maximum five-day request; no additional pages are fetched automatically.
Availability depends on location, season and Google coverage.
maps_pollen.authentication: API key required in this implementation.

maps_area_insights.purpose: Count matching places in a circle, region or polygon with Places Aggregate. This is an aggregate query rather than a count of a limited Places search page.

area.description: Exactly one of circle, region or customArea.

area.circle.description: Circular area; mutually exclusive with region/customArea.

area.circle.latLng.latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

area.circle.latLng.longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

area.region.description: An administrative/geographic region identified by a Google place resource.

area.region.place.description: Region resource in places/PLACE_ID format, not a free-form region name.

area.customArea.description: Custom polygon area; mutually exclusive with circle/region.

area.customArea.polygon.coordinates.description: Ordered ring of coordinate objects; first and last coordinates must match.

area.customArea.polygon.coordinates[].la.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

area.customArea.polygon.coordinates[].lo.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

includedTypes.description: Google place types to include, such as restaurant or cafe.

includePlaces.description: Request matching place resource IDs in addition to the count.

minRating.description: Inclusive lower rating bound; cannot exceed maxRating.

maps_area_insights.result: Google’s response with `count` (normally an int64 string) and optional `placeInsights[].place` resources when IDs were requested and available.
notes: Supply exactly one area form. Nested objects are JSON values on the CLI; their child parameters do not have independent flags.
Polygon rings must be closed. Google also checks polygon geometry, supported types, area and coverage.
Place IDs are available only for counts of 100 or less. The tool does not automatically request Place Details.
maps_area_insights.authentication: API key or OAuth for the main API.

maps_snap_to_roads.purpose: Match an ordered GPS trace to the most likely road geometry. Use Nearest Roads for independent points rather than a travelled path.

path.description: GPS coordinate objects in travel order.

path[].latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

path[].longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

interpolate.description: Add intermediate road geometry between supplied points.

maps_snap_to_roads.result: The original Roads response, including `snappedPoints` and any `warningMessage`. Points preserve road `placeId`, `location` and `originalIndex` when provided.
notes: Consecutive input points should be within about 300 metres for good matching.
Interpolated points may not have an originalIndex. Speed limits are not requested by this tool.
maps_snap_to_roads.authentication: API key required in this implementation.

maps_nearest_roads.purpose: Find nearby road segments for independent GPS points without interpreting them as one continuous trace.

points[].latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

points[].longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

maps_nearest_roads.result: The original Roads response with `snappedPoints`, road `placeId`, `location` and `originalIndex` mapping back to input points.
notes: A point can match more than one road segment; retain originalIndex rather than assuming one output per input.
Speed limits are not requested by this tool.
maps_nearest_roads.authentication: API key required in this implementation.

maps_reverse_geocode.purpose: Convert exact coordinates to the first reverse-Geocoding result. Use the result’s components when a formatted address alone is insufficient.

latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

maps_reverse_geocode.result: The first native Geocoding result, including `formatted_address`, `address_components`, `geometry` and `place_id` when available.
notes: Only the first result is returned. No match is a tool error.
maps_reverse_geocode.authentication: API key required in this implementation.

maps_search_places.purpose: Search Places (New) by text and optional location/rating/type filters. Use returned IDs for selective detail requests.

locationBias.description: Optional circular search bias; a bias is not a hard geographic restriction.

locationBias.latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

locationBias.longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

openNow.description: Restrict to places currently open when true.

minRating.description: Minimum user rating requested from Google.

includedType.description: Google place type, such as cafe.

maps_search_places.result: An array of up to 20 Google Place objects with selected search fields, Maps/source links and attribution metadata.

example.query: coffee near Gare de Lyon, Paris

notes: This tool requests one page of 20 results and does not return or automatically follow a page token.
Missing opening/rating data depends on Google coverage; do not infer an exhaustive inventory from this search.
maps_search_places.authentication: API key or OAuth for the main API.

maps_search_nearby.purpose: Find places inside a bounded radius around a resolved center. Unlike Text Search, this uses a hard circular location restriction.

center.description: Center input and the indicator describing how to interpret it.

center.value.description: Address/landmark, or a latitude,longitude string when isCoordinates is true.

center.isCoordinates.description: Treat value as exact coordinates without geocoding.

keyword.description: A Google place type passed as includedTypes, such as cafe; not an arbitrary text keyword.

openNow.description: Keep only results whose currentOpeningHours.openNow is true.

minRating.description: Minimum rating applied locally to the returned places.

maps_search_nearby.result: An array of up to 20 selected Place objects. Local opening/rating filters can reduce the array further.
notes: When filtering, missing opening status does not count as open and missing rating is treated as 0.
Address centers require location resolution; coordinates avoid that extra call.
maps_search_nearby.authentication: Places accepts API key or OAuth. Address/landmark centers also need an API key for Geocoding resolution.

maps_place_details.purpose: Expand a known place ID into selected details, reviews and optional photo URLs. Preserve author/source information and any AI disclosure text.

placeId.description: Google place ID, optionally prefixed with places/.

maxPhotos.description: Maximum photo-media URL lookups to perform.

sessionToken.description: Same-project Autocomplete (New) session token. Reuse the prediction token in this concluding request; create a fresh token for the next session.
sessionToken.default: No session token; Google bills outside an Autocomplete session

maps_place_details.result: A native Google Place object for the requested field mask. When photos are requested, `photoUrls` carries media URLs plus photo-author attribution and source links.
notes: Each selected photo can make an additional request; zero photos avoids those calls.
The tool uses a fixed details field mask, not every possible Google Place field. Unavailable fields may be absent.
maps_place_details.authentication: API key or OAuth for the main API.

maps_directions.purpose: Compute a route between two endpoints and expose both selected Google route data and normalized totals.

origin.description: Origin address/landmark or exact latitude,longitude string.

destination.description: Destination address/landmark or exact latitude,longitude string.

mode.description: Travel mode. Driving uses traffic-aware routing.

departure_time.description: Departure instant as RFC 3339 including Z or an explicit UTC offset.

avoid_tolls.description: Avoid toll roads; true is supported only for driving.

avoid_highways.description: Avoid highways; true is supported only for driving.

arrival_time.description: Desired arrival as RFC 3339 with timezone; transit mode only.

maps_directions.result: An object containing `routes`, `summary`, `total_distance` (value in metres), `total_duration` (value in seconds) and optional optimization indices. Route entries contain selected legs, steps, polyline and warnings.
notes: departure_time and arrival_time cannot both be supplied. arrival_time is accepted only for transit.
Avoidance flags require driving. Google applies additional travel-mode/time/region restrictions.
No available route is an explicit error.
maps_directions.authentication: Routes/Places accept API key or OAuth. Named-location resolution also needs an API key for Geocoding; exact coordinate strings avoid that lookup.

maps_distance_matrix.purpose: Compare travel distance and duration for every origin/destination pair. Check individual cells and errors rather than treating a successful response as complete.

origins.description: Origin strings: addresses or exact latitude,longitude pairs.

destinations.description: Destination strings: addresses or exact latitude,longitude pairs.

mode.description: Travel mode. Driving uses traffic-aware routing.

departure_time.description: Departure instant as RFC 3339 including Z or an explicit UTC offset.

avoid_tolls.description: Avoid toll roads; true is supported only for driving.

avoid_highways.description: Avoid highways; true is supported only for driving.

maps_distance_matrix.result: An object with `origin_addresses`, `destination_addresses`, row-major `distances` and `durations`, and an `errors` array. Successful cell values are metres/seconds; failed or missing cells remain null.
notes: At most 625 origin × destination pairs; transit is limited to 100 pairs.
At most 50 non-coordinate origin/destination strings in total. Per-array schema limits do not override these combined limits.
Toll/highway avoidance applies only to driving. This tool does not expose arrival_time.
A single matrix HTTP request may bill multiple elements.
maps_distance_matrix.authentication: API key or OAuth for the main API.

maps_elevation.purpose: Get geographic height for exact coordinate points.

locations.description: Coordinate objects for which to request elevation.

locations[].latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

locations[].longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

maps_elevation.result: The native Elevation `results` array. Entries can contain `elevation` in metres, `location` and `resolution`.
notes: The tool returns Google’s reported data without converting elevation units.
maps_elevation.authentication: API key required in this implementation.

maps_timezone.purpose: Resolve timezone identity and UTC/DST offsets at an instant, then derive a local timestamp.

latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

maps_timezone.result: Timezone response fields such as `timeZoneId`, `timeZoneName`, `rawOffset` and `dstOffset` in seconds, plus derived `localTime` in RFC 3339 format.
notes: The request converts milliseconds to whole seconds; sub-second precision is not preserved.
Local time uses the returned raw and DST offsets for the requested instant.
maps_timezone.authentication: API key required in this implementation.

maps_weather.purpose: Request current conditions or one page of daily/hourly forecast data for exact coordinates.

latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

type.description: Select current conditions, daily forecast or hourly forecast.

forecastDays.description: Requested daily forecast length; used only with forecast_daily.

forecastHours.description: Requested hourly forecast length; used only with forecast_hourly.

maps_weather.result: The native Weather response: current-condition fields, `forecastDays`, or `forecastHours`, depending on type. Preserve returned units, timestamps and any nextPageToken.
notes: forecastDays is ignored for other types; forecastHours is ignored outside forecast_hourly.
This tool does not automatically follow pagination tokens. The requested horizon may exceed the records in one response page.
Coverage and forecast availability depend on Google.
maps_weather.authentication: API key or OAuth for the main API.

maps_air_quality.purpose: Get current air-quality indices with optional pollutant concentrations and provider health recommendations.

latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

maps_air_quality.result: The native Air Quality current-conditions response, including indices and optional `healthRecommendations`/`pollutants` when supplied by Google.
notes: Recommendations are provider data, not a personalized medical assessment.
This tool exposes current conditions, not historical or forecast endpoints.
maps_air_quality.authentication: API key or OAuth for the main API.

maps_static_map.purpose: Render a PNG map with optional markers and path specifications.

center.description: Center as an address or latitude,longitude string.

zoom.default: Omitted; Google chooses or infers it

size.description: Pixel dimensions WIDTHxHEIGHT; runtime limits each dimension to 1–640.

markers.description: Repeated Google Static Maps marker specifications, e.g. color:red|48.8584,2.2945.

path.description: Repeated Google Static Maps path specifications, e.g. color:blue|48.8584,2.2945|48.8606,2.3376.

maps_static_map.result: MCP returns inline image/png content. CLI returns `{mimeType,base64}` JSON, or raw PNG bytes when --output is supplied.
notes: At least one of center, markers or path is required.
The complete request URL must fit within 16,384 characters. The schema’s size pattern is broader than the runtime’s 640-pixel bound.
Marker/path styling follows Google Static Maps syntax. Google attribution remains in the rendered image.
maps_static_map.authentication: API key required in this implementation.

maps_batch_geocode.purpose: Geocode a bounded list of addresses while preserving input order and each item’s success or failure.
maps_batch_geocode.result: An array in input order. Each row has `address`, `success` and either `data` (the geocode object) or `error`.
notes: Uses bounded concurrency with at most five Google requests active per process.
Item failures do not force a nonzero CLI exit status; inspect success/error on every row.
maps_batch_geocode.authentication: API key required in this implementation.

maps_explore_area.purpose: Resolve one location, search selected categories around it, and expand only the leading results in each category.

topN.description: Maximum places per category to expand with details.

maps_explore_area.result: An object with resolved `location`, `radius` and `categories`. Each category has type/count/top or an error; expanded places can contain details_error.
notes: Each category searches up to 20 places; count is the returned page count, not an aggregate inventory.
Category and detail failures remain visible within successful top-level output.
This composite makes multiple Google requests; limit categories and topN to the task.
maps_explore_area.authentication: Places accepts API key or OAuth. Named locations also need an API key for Geocoding.

maps_plan_route.purpose: Plan a single route through ordered stops, optionally asking Google to reorder intermediate stops while keeping the endpoints fixed.

stops.description: Ordered addresses/landmarks or exact latitude,longitude strings; first/last stay endpoints.

mode.description: Travel mode. Driving uses traffic-aware routing.

departure_time.description: Departure instant as RFC 3339 including Z or an explicit UTC offset.

avoid_tolls.description: Avoid toll roads; true is supported only for driving.

avoid_highways.description: Avoid highways; true is supported only for driving.

optimize.description: Request intermediate-stop optimization when more than three total stops and mode is not transit.

maps_plan_route.result: An object with `mode`, effective `optimized`, ordered resolved `stops`, display `legs`, total_distance, total_duration, polyline and warnings. Leg durationSeconds is numeric seconds.
notes: Transit supports only two endpoints and no intermediate stops.
Optimization takes effect only for four or more total stops (at least two intermediate stops).
This optimizes stop order for one route, not vehicle/task assignment across a fleet.
maps_plan_route.authentication: Routes/Places accept API key or OAuth. Named-location resolution also needs an API key for Geocoding; exact coordinate strings avoid that lookup.

maps_compare_places.purpose: Find and enrich a short list of places, optionally comparing driving distance from exact user coordinates.

userLocation.description: Exact user coordinates for optional distance comparison.

userLocation.latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

userLocation.longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

maps_compare_places.result: An object with `places` and optional `distance_error`. Places can include details/details_error, distance, drive_time and per-place distance_errors.
notes: Comparison travel is driving; this tool has no configurable travel-mode parameter.
Details and distance failures are preserved instead of dropping otherwise usable places.
Only the requested shortlist is enriched.
maps_compare_places.authentication: Places and optional Routes accept API key or OAuth.

maps_search_along_route.purpose: Compute a route and search Places using its encoded polyline, rather than approximating the journey with one circular search.

textQuery.description: Places query for stops along the route, such as cafes or charging stations.

origin.description: Route origin address/landmark or exact latitude,longitude string.

destination.description: Route destination address/landmark or exact latitude,longitude string.

mode.description: Travel mode for the route used by the search.

maxResults.description: Maximum Places results requested in the response page.

maps_search_along_route.result: An object with `places`, optional `routingSummaries`, and the computed `route` including selected Google route data and normalized totals.
notes: The default mode is walking, unlike directions, matrix and plan-route, which default to driving.
No automatic pagination or Place Details expansion is performed.
This tool does not expose the departure/arrival or avoidance parameters of directions.
maps_search_along_route.authentication: Routes/Places accept API key or OAuth. Named-location resolution also needs an API key for Geocoding; exact coordinate strings avoid that lookup.

maps_local_rank_tracker.purpose: Measure a target place’s appearance within the first 20 Text Search results at each point of a geographic grid.

keyword.description: Single search keyword; use keyword or keywords.

keywords.description: One to three search keywords; takes precedence if both keyword forms are supplied.

placeId.description: Target place ID, optionally prefixed with places/.

center.description: Exact center of the scan grid.

center.latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive.

center.longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive.

gridSize.description: Number of rows and columns; all integer values 3–7 are accepted.

gridSpacing.description: Distance in metres between neighboring grid points.

maps_local_rank_tracker.result: An object with target, grid_size, grid_spacing_m and per-keyword metrics/grid. ARP averages found ranks; ATRP uses rank 21 for successful queries where the target was absent; SoLV is the percentage of successful points ranked in the top 3. failed_points and found_in expose coverage.
notes: At least one of keyword or keywords is required; individual schema rows do not express that alternative.
Search requests scale as keyword count × gridSize² (up to 147 before retries).
Failed points are excluded from rank metrics, not treated as valid misses. Metrics can be null when no usable observations exist.
A search rank is not the target’s user-review rating. Results are samples from biased text searches, not guarantees of a user’s Google Maps ranking.
maps_local_rank_tracker.authentication: API key or OAuth for the main API.

maps_datasets.summary: Manage geospatial datasets for Google Maps data-driven styling, including asynchronous imports from an existing Cloud Storage object.
maps_datasets.purpose: Manage geospatial datasets for Google Maps data-driven styling, including asynchronous imports from an existing Cloud Storage object.

operation.description: Select list, get, create, update, delete, import, download or fetch_errors. Create/update/delete/import modify cloud resources.

parent.description: projects/{project ID or number}; required for list and create.

name.description: projects/{project}/datasets/{dataset}; required except list/create. Only get also accepts @active to inspect the latest completed version.

dataset.description: Native Dataset JSON for create/update; Google validates the official schema. Create requires a unique displayName and usage:["USAGE_DATA_DRIVEN_STYLING"]. Update forwards metadata and injects the matching resource name.

gcsSource.description: Cloud Storage source for import; the caller must already have access to the object. No local files are read by this tool.

gcsSource.inputUri.description: Existing gs://bucket/object URI. The caller needs storage.objects.get, for example Storage Object Viewer.

gcsSource.fileFormat.description: Source encoding: FILE_FORMAT_GEOJSON, FILE_FORMAT_KML or FILE_FORMAT_CSV.

versionDescription.description: Description for the new imported data version. Used only by import.

updateMask.description: Comma-separated native metadata field paths for update, for example description,displayName.

pageSize.description: Maximum datasets/errors to return in one page; wrapper accepts 1–500.

pageToken.description: Token from the preceding list/fetch_errors result. Keep other request arguments unchanged.

tag.description: For list, active returns each dataset’s latest completed version and skips datasets with none.
tag.default: Latest version regardless of processing state

maps_datasets.result: Native Dataset/list/error JSON, import version resource name, or downloaded source bytes with MIME type and cache headers. get preserves status.state, status.errorMessage and versionId; importing does not mean processing has completed.
notes: [Official REST resource and native Dataset schema](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/datasets/reference/rest/v1/projects.datasets). Permissions include mapsplatformdatasets.datasets.list/get/create/update/delete/import/export, according to the operation.

[GCS import](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/datasets/create) creates a new version asynchronously. Call get explicitly to inspect status; fetch_errors retrieves processing errors. The tool never polls automatically.
Google’s current public v1 REST API does not document listVersions. Use get (latest), get with @active, and returned versionId; complete version history enumeration is not claimed.
[Download media](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/datasets/reference/rest/v1/media/download) requires mapsplatformdatasets.datasets.export. CLI --output writes downloaded bytes.

[Maps Datasets API has no usage charge](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/datasets/overview), but requires a configured Cloud project; Google Maps display and Cloud Storage may have their own charges and terms. Data-driven styling is the supported usage. Local multipart upload is not exposed; use an existing GCS object.
maps_datasets.authentication: OAuth 2.0 only, using a service account or ADC and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform. API keys are not accepted. Configure the resource project and quota-project permissions separately.

maps_route_optimization.summary: Optimize delivery or service fleets with the actual Route Optimization API and an intact native ShipmentModel, including capacities, time windows and cost constraints.
maps_route_optimization.purpose: Optimize delivery or service fleets with the actual Route Optimization API and an intact native ShipmentModel, including capacities, time windows and cost constraints.

operation.description: optimize solves synchronously; validate sets solvingMode=VALIDATE_ONLY; batch creates a GCS-backed job; optimize_long_running and optimize_uri create experimental jobs; get_operation reads one status.

parent.description: projects/{project ID}; optionally /locations/-. Synchronous and long-running optimization reject regional location IDs. Batch/URI accept the native location form.

name.description: Exact projects/{project}[/locations/{location}]/operations/{ID} returned by Google. Used only for get_operation.

request.description: Complete native request object, without parent. For optimize/validate/optimize_long_running supply model with shipments/vehicles and all needed native constraints; Google validates the full schema. Batch requires 1–100 modelConfigs with inputConfig.gcsSource.uri, outputConfig.gcsDestination.uri and JSON or PROTO_TEXT dataFormat. URI requires input.uri/output.uri as gs:// paths ending .json or .txtpb.

maps_route_optimization.result: Native OptimizeToursResponse or long-running Operation JSON. Polling preserves done:false, metadata, and completed response/error objects without hiding failed-operation status.
notes: [Native optimizeTours request/ShipmentModel reference](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/route-optimization/reference/rest/v1/projects/optimizeTours). validate still calls Google; it does not solve the fleet model.

[IAM setup](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/route-optimization/cloud-setup): roles/routeoptimization.viewer permits OptimizeTours and reading operations; roles/routeoptimization.editor also permits batch jobs. Permissions include routeoptimization.locations.use, routeoptimization.operations.create/get. The API must be enabled on the project.

[Batch jobs](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/route-optimization/reference/rest/v1/projects/batchOptimizeTours) read inputs and write outputs in Cloud Storage. Supply explicit object URIs and storage permissions; jobs can continue after the CLI/MCP request ends. No files are uploaded and no automatic polling occurs.

[Long-running and URI variants are experimental](https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis/blob/master/google/maps/routeoptimization/v1/route_optimization_service.proto); URI uses the documented case-sensitive :OptimizeToursUri endpoint. Google may change pre-GA behavior.

[Operation cancel, delete and list are currently unsupported by Google](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/route-optimization/reference/rest/v1/operations). This tool therefore exposes get_operation only; no cancellation guarantee is made.

[Billing](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/route-optimization/usage-and-billing) depends on shipments and the Single Vehicle Routing or Fleet Routing SKU. This is separate from Routes API waypoint optimization. Transport timeouts do not cancel jobs.
maps_route_optimization.authentication: OAuth 2.0 only, using a service account or ADC and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform. API keys are not accepted. Configure the resource project and quota-project permissions separately.

maps_air_quality_forecast.summary: Retrieve hourly air quality forecasts for an explicit time or interval, up to 96 hours ahead.
maps_air_quality_forecast.purpose: Retrieve hourly air quality forecasts for an explicit time or interval, up to 96 hours ahead.

dateTime.description: Single RFC3339 UTC Z timestamp; Google rounds it down to the preceding hour. Mutually exclusive with period and hours.

period.description: Inclusive hourly time interval; ordered and bounded to 96 forecast hours or 720 historical hours. Mutually exclusive with dateTime and hours.

period.startTime.description: Interval start in valid RFC3339 UTC notation ending Z.

period.endTime.description: Inclusive interval end in valid RFC3339 UTC notation ending Z.

pageSize.description: Maximum hourly records in this page; wrapper caps forecast at 96 and history at Google’s maximum of 168.

pageToken.description: nextPageToken from a preceding request; keep other request fields unchanged.

universalAqi.description: Include the Universal Air Quality Index.

languageCode.description: IETF language code for available localized text; Google chooses the closest supported language.

uaqiColorPalette.description: Universal AQI palette: RED_GREEN, INDIGO_PERSIAN_DARK or INDIGO_PERSIAN_LIGHT. Local index palettes remain fixed.

extraComputations.description: Request LOCAL_AQI, HEALTH_RECOMMENDATIONS, POLLUTANT_ADDITIONAL_INFO, DOMINANT_POLLUTANT_CONCENTRATION and/or POLLUTANT_CONCENTRATION.

customLocalAqis.description: Override the local index selected for particular ISO country/region codes.

customLocalAqis[].regionCode.description: Two-letter country/region code receiving the AQI override.

customLocalAqis[].aqi.description: Supported local AQI code, for example us_epa. Google validates supported combinations.

maps_air_quality_forecast.result: Google’s native hourlyForecasts, regionCode and nextPageToken, including optional pollutant and health fields.
notes: [Forecast request reference](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/air-quality/reference/rest/v1/forecast/lookup). Choose dateTime or period.
Exactly one time selector is required. Timestamp syntax and interval order/maximum span are validated locally; Google validates current availability and geographic coverage.
One page is returned per call. Follow nextPageToken explicitly; all native indexes, concentrations, recommendations and region metadata are preserved.

[Air Quality policies](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/air-quality/policies) apply, including attribution, display and caching requirements. Coverage and local index availability vary by country.
maps_air_quality_forecast.authentication: API key or OAuth 2.0 bearer token with cloud-platform scope; enable the named API and billing. With OAuth, the quota-project principal needs serviceusage.services.use.

maps_air_quality_history.summary: Retrieve historical air quality information from the previous 30 days.
maps_air_quality_history.purpose: Retrieve historical air quality information from the previous 30 days.

dateTime.description: Single RFC3339 UTC Z timestamp; Google rounds it down to the preceding hour. Mutually exclusive with period and hours.

period.description: Inclusive hourly time interval; ordered and bounded to 96 forecast hours or 720 historical hours. Mutually exclusive with dateTime and hours.

period.startTime.description: Interval start in valid RFC3339 UTC notation ending Z.

period.endTime.description: Inclusive interval end in valid RFC3339 UTC notation ending Z.

maps_map_tiles.purpose: Create Map Tiles sessions and retrieve 2D, photorealistic 3D, and Street View resources for a map viewer. This is a retrieval interface, not a renderer. Google licenses Map Tiles for visualization only, prohibiting machine interpretation, image analysis, object detection, geodata extraction and offline use.

operation.description: create_session, tile_2d, viewport, root_3d, resource_3d, streetview_pano_ids, streetview_metadata, streetview_thumbnail or streetview_tile. Selects the endpoint and required arguments.

sessionOptions.description: Required for create_session. Native createSession options; mapType, language and region are mandatory.
sessionOptions.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

sessionOptions.mapType.description: roadmap, satellite, terrain or streetview. terrain requires layerTypes containing layerRoadmap.
sessionOptions.mapType.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

sessionOptions.language.description: IETF language tag such as en-US.
sessionOptions.language.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

sessionOptions.region.description: Two uppercase CLDR region letters, such as US; the physical location of the user.
sessionOptions.region.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

sessionOptions.imageFormat.description: jpeg or png tile encoding. JPEG does not support transparent overlays.

sessionOptions.scale.description: scaleFactor1x, scaleFactor2x or scaleFactor4x controls map element size.

sessionOptions.highDpi.description: Increase pixel dimensions with 2x/4x scale; has no effect at 1x.

sessionOptions.overlay.description: Render requested layerTypes without base imagery when true.

sessionOptions.layerTypes.description: One to three values from layerRoadmap, layerStreetview and layerTraffic. terrain requires layerRoadmap.

sessionOptions.styles.description: Native Google map-style JSON objects. Valid only for roadmap. See https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/style-reference .

session.description: The returned createSession session token. Required for every 2D and Street View request, but not 3D. Follow the response expiry rather than assuming a fixed lifetime.
session.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

zoom.description: Integer zoom: 0..22 for tile_2d/viewport; 0..5 for streetview_tile. Availability varies; use viewport metadata for the maximum available zoom.
zoom.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

x.description: Tile column for tile_2d or streetview_tile. 2D requires x < 2^zoom; Street View bounds depend on panorama dimensions in metadata.
x.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

y.description: Tile row for tile_2d or streetview_tile. 2D requires y < 2^zoom; Street View bounds depend on panorama dimensions in metadata.
y.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

north.description: Required viewport northern latitude in WGS84 degrees; must exceed south.
north.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

south.description: Required viewport southern latitude in WGS84 degrees.
south.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

east.description: Required viewport eastern longitude. A negative east with positive west can cross the antimeridian.
east.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

west.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

resourceUrl.description: For resource_3d, an absolute Google-issued https://tile.googleapis.com/v1/3dtiles/... URL from a tileset. No custom origin, port, userinfo, fragment or encoded path segments. Returned API-key query parameters are discarded and configured credentials are applied.
resourceUrl.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

panoId.description: Required for streetview_tile/thumbnail, or an alternative to latitude+longitude for streetview_metadata. IDs are transient and should not be relied on beyond one user session.
panoId.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

latitude.description: For streetview_metadata, latitude of the search center; requires longitude and excludes panoId.
latitude.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

longitude.description: For streetview_metadata, longitude of the search center; requires latitude and excludes panoId.
longitude.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

locations.description: For streetview_pano_ids, one to 100 native location objects, each containing lat and lng.
locations.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

locations[].lat.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

locations[].lng.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

radius.description: Street View search radius in meters for pano_ids or metadata coordinate search. This implementation accepts 0..100000. Cannot accompany a metadata panoId.

fov.description: Thumbnail horizontal field of view, 30..120 degrees.

maps_map_tiles.result: Native Google JSON for sessions, viewport, panorama lookup/metadata, 3D root and child JSON tilesets; attribution, copyrights, reportProblemLink and session expiry are preserved. Tiles, thumbnails and non-JSON 3D resources return binary content with MIME type plus cache-control/ETag metadata. MCP inlines supported images; other resources use base64 JSON. CLI --output writes the original bytes.
notes: Operation contracts: create_session needs sessionOptions; tile_2d needs session/zoom/x/y; viewport needs session/zoom/north/south/east/west; root_3d takes no other fields; resource_3d needs resourceUrl; streetview_pano_ids needs session/locations; streetview_metadata needs session plus panoId OR latitude+longitude; streetview_thumbnail needs session/panoId; streetview_tile needs session/panoId/zoom/x/y. Unused operation fields are rejected.

create_session obtains a Google session and is not retried automatically. Panorama lookups are read-only POST requests. A downstream viewer must implement stitching/3D rendering; this tool does not include a web or native renderer.

Map Tiles policy prohibits unauthorized prefetching, indexing, storage and caching; respect Cache-Control, ETag and your agreement. Use only for map visualization. See https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/policies . Do not submit imagery to agents for image interpretation or geodata extraction.

Display the Google Maps logo and provider attribution. Use viewport copyright for 2D maps, and streetview_metadata copyright plus its Report a problem link for Street View. A 3D renderer must display tile copyright attribution. Do not crop or hide credits.

Coverage, EEA terms/functionality, billing and quotas vary. Native session expiry is authoritative. Panorama IDs are short-lived. No tile cache, bulk area download, offline map or image-analysis operation is implemented.

Primary contracts: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/session_tokens ; https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/2d-tiles-overview ; https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/streetview ; https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/3d-tiles .
maps_map_tiles.authentication: API key or OAuth with cloud-platform scope and a billed quota project. Enable Map Tiles API. Service accounts are supported by Google for Map Tiles; quota-project Service Usage permissions are required. See https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/get-api-key .

maps_streetview.purpose: Inspect Street View panorama metadata or retrieve a static JPEG image at a location or panorama ID. Metadata can establish imagery availability before a billed image request.

operation.description: metadata or image. Metadata returns JSON; image returns JPEG bytes.

location.description: Address, latitude/longitude string (for example 48.8584,2.2945), or place_id:PLACE_ID. Exactly one of location and panoId is required.
location.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

panoId.description: Specific panorama ID; mutually exclusive with location. Panorama IDs can change, so retain the original search location to refresh them.
panoId.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

width.description: Image width in pixels, 1..640. Used only by image. Larger images requiring special Google access are outside this implementation.

height.description: Image height in pixels, 1..640. Used only by image.

heading.description: Image camera compass heading in degrees, 0..360.
heading.default: Google points toward the supplied location

fov.description: Image horizontal field of view, 1..120 degrees.

radius.description: Search radius in meters. This implementation accepts integer 0..100000.

source.description: Search source: default, google or outdoor. Availability depends on the collection and region.

returnErrorCode.description: For image, return an HTTP error instead of the gray no-imagery placeholder.

signature.description: Optional URL signature for the exact encoded request. Google recommends signing and requires it for some accounts. This tool forwards a supplied signature; it does not generate one. For signed requests the executable appends signature last, after the API key. Sign the exact encoded unsigned path/query including generated defaults. Image order: location, radius, source, pano, size, heading, fov, pitch, return_error_code, key (omitted optional fields are skipped); metadata omits image fields. Spaces encode as +. Defaults are size=640x400 and return_error_code=true.

maps_streetview.result: Native panorama metadata JSON, including status, date, location, pano_id and copyright when available; or JPEG bytes with MIME type and safe HTTP cache metadata. A missing image is an error by default. CLI --output saves bytes; MCP exposes an image plus metadata.
notes: Exactly one of location and panoId is required. Width, height, heading, fov, pitch and returnErrorCode are used only by image. Unused operation arguments are rejected.
Metadata requests are currently free of charge and do not consume Street View image quota; image requests are billed. See https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/streetview/metadata .

Keep the embedded Google Maps attribution intact. Street View imagery may not be used for print, and Maps storage/caching restrictions apply. This tool does not grant a license to retain, redistribute or analyze imagery. See https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/streetview/policies and https://about.google/brand-resource-center/products-and-services/geo-guidelines/ .

Native image requests and optional signatures follow https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/streetview/request-streetview . Signing is forwarded only; premium-sized imagery and URL-signing-key configuration are not implemented.
Coverage and EEA terms vary by project and location. Panorama IDs and capture dates can change or be unavailable.
maps_streetview.authentication: API key required for Street View Static in this implementation; OAuth-only credentials cannot call it. Enable Street View Static API. Google recommends a digital signature, required in some account configurations.

maps_streetview_publish.purpose: Manage photos and photo sequences belonging to the consenting Google user. Supports the complete documented v1 REST method set plus bounded photo-byte upload. Publishing and deletion are explicit caller-controlled operations and are never retried automatically.

operation.description: list, get, start_upload, upload, create, update, delete, batch_get, batch_update, batch_delete, list_sequences, get_sequence, start_sequence_upload, create_sequence or delete_sequence.

photoId.description: Google photo ID for get, update or delete. Pass the ID only, without resource paths or URL parameters.
photoId.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

sequenceId.description: Google sequence ID for get_sequence or delete_sequence. The create operation name carries the sequence ID.
sequenceId.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

photoIds.description: One to 100 photo IDs for batch_get or batch_delete.
photoIds.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

view.description: BASIC or INCLUDE_DOWNLOAD_URL for list, get, batch_get or get_sequence. Download URLs are sensitive user-resource URLs; this tool does not fetch them.

languageCode.description: Preferred language tag for list, get or batch_get photo metadata.

pageSize.description: Requested page size, 1..100, for list or list_sequences. Google may return fewer items.

pageToken.description: Opaque nextPageToken from a previous list or list_sequences response. Pagination is explicit; the tool does not fetch every page.
pageToken.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

filter.description: Native Google filter expression for list, list_sequences or get_sequence; endpoint-specific grammar applies. See the official method reference.
filter.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

updateMask.description: Required comma-separated native Google FieldMask for update, for example pose.heading or pose.latLngPair.
updateMask.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

photo.description: Native Google Photo JSON for create/update. create requires uploadReference.uploadUrl from start_upload after successful byte upload; update requires photoId separately and updateMask. Photo schema: https://developers.google.com/streetview/publish/reference/rest/v1/photo .
photo.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

photoSequence.description: Native Google PhotoSequence JSON for create_sequence. Requires uploadReference.uploadUrl; include required GPS/CAMM/IMU and capture metadata for the media format. Schema: https://developers.google.com/streetview/publish/reference/rest/v1/photoSequence/create .
photoSequence.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

updatePhotoRequests.description: One to 100 native UpdatePhotoRequest objects for batch_update. Each needs photo.photoId.id and updateMask. Schema: https://developers.google.com/streetview/publish/reference/rest/v1/photos/batchUpdate .
updatePhotoRequests.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

inputType.description: Required for create_sequence: VIDEO or XDM.
inputType.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

uploadUrl.description: Exact HTTPS UploadRef URL returned by start_upload or start_sequence_upload. Only streetviewpublish.googleapis.com/media/user/{account}/photo/{reference} (or photoSequence) is accepted; no redirects, custom origins, userinfo, fragments or encoded path segments.
uploadUrl.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

dataBase64.description: Standard padded base64 of media bytes for upload. Decoded size must be 1 byte to 8 MiB. This is an implementation bound, not Google’s product limit.
dataBase64.default: Not supplied; required for the operations described

mimeType.description: Media Content-Type for upload: image/jpeg, video/mp4 or application/octet-stream.

maps_streetview_publish.result: Unmodified native Google Photo, list/pagination, UploadRef, batch result, or long-running Operation JSON as appropriate; successful empty upload/delete responses become {}. Photos retain publication status and ownership metadata. Sequence operations can remain pending; call get_sequence to inspect progress. No automatic polling, mutation or publishing occurs.
notes: Photo lifecycle: start_upload -> upload the returned URL with dataBase64 -> create with photo.uploadReference.uploadUrl and required metadata. Uploading bytes alone does not publish a photo. Images must satisfy Google’s 360-degree Photo Sphere/XMP and publishing acceptance criteria: https://developers.google.com/streetview/publish/first-app .

Photo updates use PUT and updateMask; updating photo pixels is unsupported by Google. delete and batch_delete remove the user’s published photos. No write, publish, upload or delete is part of doctor or live smoke checks.

Sequence lifecycle: start_sequence_upload -> upload -> create_sequence(inputType, photoSequence) -> get_sequence. Actual large video uploads commonly exceed this CLI/MCP 8 MiB limit; resumable/chunked uploads are not implemented. Use Google’s upload flow externally when larger media is necessary, then pass its UploadRef to create_sequence. Metadata/list/get/delete sequence endpoints remain available.

Native objects use Google’s official schemas rather than duplicating complex GPS, pose, IMU, connections and place fields. Unknown top-level tool arguments are rejected; endpoint-specific nested semantics are validated by Google. Every batch_update entry must include photo.photoId.id and updateMask.

All documented v1 REST endpoints are implemented: photo create/delete/get/startUpload/update; photos list/batchGet/batchUpdate/batchDelete; photoSequence create/delete/get/startUpload; photoSequences list. Reference: https://developers.google.com/streetview/publish/reference/rest . This does not mean every accepted native nested field was tested live.

Upload requests are fixed-origin, bounded, non-retrying POSTs; all mutations disable automatic retries because ambiguous network failures could otherwise duplicate public changes. Review operation results explicitly.

Google ownership, privacy, copyright, 360-imagery acceptance, processing and quota restrictions apply. End-user consent and ownership cannot be replaced by service-account IAM permissions. See https://developers.google.com/streetview/publish/authorizing .

Publish operations have not been live-tested with the supplied service-account credential: a real consenting user credential is required, and public mutations are deliberately excluded from smoke tests.
maps_streetview_publish.authentication: End-user OAuth only, with https://www.googleapis.com/auth/streetviewpublish scope granted by the user. Use explicit authorized_user credentials in GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS and OAuth mode; a service-account key, implicit ADC or API key alone is rejected for this tool. Configure the OAuth client consent flow separately; this executable refreshes authorized-user credentials but does not host a browser consent callback.

maps_speed_limits.purpose: Get posted automobile speed limits for road segments using a GPS path or IDs returned by Roads snapping/nearest-road calls. This restricted Google feature requires Asset Tracking access; enabling the Roads API alone is insufficient.

path.description: One to 100 GPS coordinates; mutually exclusive with roadPlaceIds. Google snaps this path before looking up segment limits.

path[].latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees, from -90 to 90.

path[].longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees, from -180 to 180.

roadPlaceIds.description: One to 100 road-segment place IDs from maps_snap_to_roads or maps_nearest_roads; ordinary business/place IDs may have no speed-limit data. Mutually exclusive with path.

units.description: Return kilometers per hour (KPH) or miles per hour (MPH).

maps_speed_limits.result: The complete native Roads response, including speedLimits entries (placeId, speedLimit, units), optional snappedPoints for path requests, warnings and other Google metadata.
notes: Restricted access: Google documents an Asset Tracking license requirement. Transitioned Premium Plan projects with Asset Tracking capabilities may retain access. An enabled API or ordinary billing account does not establish entitlement. https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/roads/speed-limits
Each returned speedLimits entry triggers the Roads Speed Limits SKU; one HTTP request can incur multiple billable entries. Request the smallest useful batch.
For variable limits Google returns the maximum automobile limit. Data is not real-time and can be missing, estimated, inaccurate or outdated; consult posted signs and applicable safety requirements.

A 403 retains the sanitized Google reason and adds an access hint. API enablement, key restrictions and permissions can also cause rejection; the executable does not label every 403 a license failure.
maps_speed_limits.authentication: API key required in this implementation, including when OAuth mode is selected. Roads Speed Limits entitlement is separate from credentials.

maps_autocomplete.purpose: Get Places API (New) predictions while a user types. Supports place and query predictions, geographic bias/restriction, regional/type filters, cursor position and caller-managed billing session tokens.

input.description: Non-empty query text, including partial place names or addresses.

locationBias.description: Prefer results around exactly one circle or rectangle; results may fall outside it. Cannot coexist with locationRestriction.
locationBias.default: Google IP bias if neither geographic option is supplied

locationRestriction.description: Restrict results to exactly one circle or rectangle. Cannot coexist with locationBias.
locationRestriction.default: Google IP bias if neither geographic option is supplied

includedPrimaryTypes.description: Up to five primary place types. The special (cities) or (regions) collection must be the sole entry.

includedRegionCodes.description: Up to 15 two-letter CLDR region codes; intersected with locationRestriction when both are supplied. An empty array does not restrict results.

languageCode.description: Preferred IETF BCP-47 response language. Mixed-language predictions may still occur.

regionCode.description: Two-letter CLDR region used for formatting/ranking; does not restrict results to that region.

origin.description: Reference coordinate for returned geodesic distanceMeters.

inputOffset.description: Zero-based Unicode character cursor offset; must not exceed the number of characters in input.

includeQueryPredictions.description: Include query predictions as well as place predictions.

sessionToken.description: Caller-generated URL-safe token of at most 36 ASCII characters; a fresh UUID v4 is recommended for each session. Forward the same token to the concluding Place Details or Address Validation call.

includePureServiceAreaBusinesses.description: Include businesses that visit/deliver to customers and have no public business location.

includeFutureOpeningBusinesses.description: Include businesses that will open in the future.

locationBias.circle.description: Circular area; mutually exclusive with rectangle.

locationBias.circle.radius.description: Radius in meters, at most 50,000; must be positive for locationRestriction.

locationBias.rectangle.description: Closed latitude/longitude viewport; mutually exclusive with circle. Longitude bounds may cross the antimeridian.

locationBias.rectangle.low.latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; low must not exceed high.

locationBias.rectangle.low.longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; low greater than high indicates antimeridian crossing.

locationBias.rectangle.high.latitude.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; low must not exceed high.

locationBias.rectangle.high.longitude.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; low greater than high indicates antimeridian crossing.

locationRestriction.circle.description: Circular area; mutually exclusive with rectangle.

locationRestriction.circle.radius.description: Radius in meters, at most 50,000; must be positive for locationRestriction.

locationRestriction.rectangle.description: Closed latitude/longitude viewport; mutually exclusive with circle. Longitude bounds may cross the antimeridian.

locationRestriction.rectangle.low.latitu.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; low must not exceed high.

locationRestriction.rectangle.low.longit.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; low greater than high indicates antimeridian crossing.

locationRestriction.rectangle.high.latit.description: WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; low must not exceed high.

locationRestriction.rectangle.high.longi.description: WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; low greater than high indicates antimeridian crossing.

maps_autocomplete.result: Complete native suggestions response, including placePrediction/queryPrediction, text match offsets, structured formatting, place IDs, optional distanceMeters and any response metadata. No field mask removes content.
notes: Official native request fields and supported place types: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/reference/rest/v1/places/autocomplete

Tokens are caller-managed: the executable does not create or conclude sessions automatically. All requests in a session must use credentials from the same Google Cloud project; terminate with a qualifying Place Details or Address Validation request and use a fresh token next time. Missing/reused tokens can lead to per-request billing.
Circle radii are at most 50,000m; restriction circles require a positive radius. Rectangle latitude bounds must be ordered; antimeridian-crossing longitude ranges are supported.
Retain any Google Maps/provider attribution when displaying results. Regional/EEA service terms and field availability may differ.
maps_autocomplete.authentication: API key or OAuth (Places/cloud-platform scope) for the main API.

maps_geolocate.purpose: Estimate device location from observed cellular towers or WiFi access points using the complete native Google Geolocation JSON body.

body.description: Native Google request object. Supports homeMobileCountryCode, homeMobileNetworkCode, radioType (gsm/cdma/wcdma/lte/nr), carrier, considerIp, cellTowers and wifiAccessPoints, including radio-specific cellId/newRadioCellId and signal fields. See the linked Google request reference for the complete nested schema. An empty object permits server-IP fallback.

maps_geolocate.result: Google location.lat/location.lng and accuracy (uncertainty radius in meters), plus any additional native response fields.
notes: Complete radio and WiFi field descriptions, ranges and examples: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/geolocation/requests-geolocation

Google defaults considerIp to true. With no usable radio observations, fallback locates the executable/server egress IP, not the person operating the agent. Set body.considerIp=false to prohibit fallback.

WiFi positioning requires at least two physically distinct stationary access points. Google excludes locally administered/reserved MAC address ranges; mobile hotspots and invalid observations may not yield a result.
The body is intentionally extensible for native radio payloads; validation of its detailed protocol-specific fields is delegated to Google. The outer tool schema rejects unknown wrapper parameters.
A location estimate is approximate and can fail with NOT_FOUND; inspect accuracy before using the coordinates.
maps_geolocate.authentication: API key required in this implementation. The documented www.googleapis.com endpoint receives the key as a query parameter even for POST.

maps_solar.purpose: Use all three principal Solar methods: nearby building insights, regional raster data-layer metadata, and bounded GeoTIFF downloads by asset ID.

operation.description: building_insights, data_layers or geo_tiff. Each operation accepts only its relevant parameters.

location.description: Coordinate of the building search or regional data-layer center; required for building_insights and data_layers.

requiredQuality.description: Minimum imagery quality HIGH, MEDIUM or BASE for insights/data layers. BASE uses enhanced satellite imagery; geographic availability varies.

exactQualityRequired.description: Require the exact selected imagery quality instead of accepting higher quality. Valid for insights/data layers.

experiments.description: Optional EXPANDED_COVERAGE experiment for insights/data layers; Google classifies these requests as pre-GA.

additionalInsights.description: Optional DETECTED_ARRAYS for building_insights to retrieve detected rooftop solar arrays.

radiusMeters.description: Positive regional radius, required for data_layers. At most 1,000m; values over 100 must be <= pixelSizeMeters × 1,000, and values over 175 require a view without monthly flux or hourly shade.

view.description: Data-layer subset: DSM_LAYER, IMAGERY_LAYERS, IMAGERY_AND_ANNUAL_FLUX_LAYERS, IMAGERY_AND_ALL_FLUX_LAYERS or FULL_LAYERS.

pixelSizeMeters.description: Minimum data-layer pixel scale, one of 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 or 1.0 meters. Individual layers may have coarser native resolution.

id.description: Opaque asset ID taken from the id query parameter of a returned Solar data-layer URL. Required only for geo_tiff; pass an ID, not a URL.

maps_solar.result: building_insights/data_layers return the full native Google JSON including imagery dates, quality, solar potential and temporary raster URLs. Credentials are removed from returned URLs. geo_tiff returns bounded binary data with its actual MIME type and retained HTTP cache/attribution metadata; CLI JSON uses base64.
notes: Method references: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/solar/reference/rest/v1/buildingInsights/findClosest ; https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/solar/reference/rest/v1/dataLayers/get ; https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/solar/reference/rest/v1/geoTiff/get

Coverage and imagery quality vary by country/location. Building search can return NOT_FOUND when there is no building within approximately 50m. https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/solar/coverage

Data-layer URLs are temporary and still require authenticated access. Copy only their id into operation geo_tiff; the executable always downloads from solar.googleapis.com/v1/geoTiff:get and never follows arbitrary URLs.

GeoTIFF responses remain subject to the executable response-size limit (16 MiB), request budget and tool deadline. Large rasters may need a smaller radius/coarser pixel scale. Raster decoding/solar-installation design is outside this adapter.
EXPANDED_COVERAGE requests are pre-GA. EEA billing projects can have different terms and omitted content: https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/solar
Solar endpoints have distinct billing/quotas; enabling the service does not make requests free. Preserve Google Maps attribution when displaying Google content.
maps_solar.authentication: API key or OAuth (cloud-platform scope). Service-account callers also need API enablement and quota-project serviceusage.services.use.

maps_aerial_view.purpose: Retrieve an existing Aerial View video’s short-lived playback URLs or metadata without downloading the video.

operation.description: lookup retrieves playback URLs and metadata (billable); metadata retrieves available video data excluding playback URLs (free-to-call Google method).

address.description: Supported US postal address. Supply exactly one of address or videoId.

videoId.description: Previously returned Aerial View video ID. Supply exactly one of videoId or address.

maps_aerial_view.result: The native Google response, including processing/active state, available video metadata and, for active lookup responses, playback URIs grouped by format/resolution. Metadata lookup omits playback URIs.
notes: Aerial View accepts only supported US postal addresses where Google can render 3D videos. Missing videos return NOT_FOUND; use the separate maps_render_aerial_video action to request a render.
Use metadata to check state without requesting billable playback URLs. lookup itself is a billable event; poll metadata at a reasonable interval while a render is processing.

Playback URIs expire quickly; obtain fresh URIs for each display. Google prohibits downloading, storing or caching these videos. This tool returns URLs without fetching them. Video IDs may be stored under the documented caching exception. https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/aerial-view/lookup-video
Keep Google Maps attribution visible during playback. EEA terms/functionality may differ. https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/aerial-view/policies
maps_aerial_view.authentication: API key required in this implementation, including when OAuth mode is selected.

maps_render_aerial_video.purpose: Explicitly queue an asynchronous Aerial View video render for a supported US postal address; kept separate from read-only lookup so agents can recognize the upstream mutation.

address.description: Supported US postal address to render.

maps_render_aerial_video.result: The native render response with state and any available video metadata. PROCESSING means the render is queued/in progress; an existing video can return ACTIVE metadata immediately.
notes: This action changes Google’s render queue. It is not automatically retried after a transient failure, does not wait for completion, and never downloads the resulting video.
Check progress using maps_aerial_view operation metadata with the address or returned videoId; use lookup only when playback URLs are needed.

US/3D coverage, quotas and Google service terms apply; API enablement does not guarantee that an address can be rendered. https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/aerial-view/reference/rest/v1/videos/renderVideo
Do not download, store or cache Aerial View videos; display current short-lived playback URLs with required attribution.
maps_render_aerial_video.authentication: API key required in this implementation, including when OAuth mode is selected.
